# Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection
**Case:** mta-2024-11-26 | **Capture:** 2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap (21.3 MB) | **Analyst tools:** tshark, Suricata alert export

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** |
| Logged-in domain user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ traffic to the DC) |
| Windows/AD domain | NEMOTODES / nemotoads.health (DC: NEMOTODES-DC / NEMOTODE-DC, 10.11.26.3) |

Evidence: NBNS name registrations for `DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>` and `NEMOTODES<00>` from 10.11.26.183; Kerberos CNameString `oboomwald` on TGT/TGS exchanges between 10.11.26.183 and DC 10.11.26.3; Ethernet source `d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b` on all frames sourced from 10.11.26.183.

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager remote-access tool abused as a trojan/RAT).

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET fired exact NetSupport RAT rules against this host's traffic:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (65 hits)
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (2 hits)
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` (65 hits, request) / `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response` (4 hits, reply)
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` (against `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`)

This is further corroborated behaviorally: the C2 traffic uses NetSupport's characteristic plaintext check-in protocol, observed directly in HTTP POST bodies to the C2 host — `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex-encoded ciphertext>` — repeated on a near-fixed ~60-second beacon interval starting at 08:50:45 UTC+4 and continuing through at least 09:43:29 UTC+4 (dozens of check-ins captured).

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in this capture)

### Infection chain (pre-C2)
- `10.11.26.183` established a TLS session (SNI: **classicgrand.com**, resolved to **213.246.109.5**) at 08:50:11 — likely the malvertising/redirect landing page.
- Immediately after, a TLS session to SNI **modandcrackedapk.com** (resolved to **193.42.38.139**) at 08:50:14 — a fake cracked-software site, matching Suricata alert `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)`. This is consistent with a "cracked software" lure delivering the NetSupport RAT installer. Both sessions are TLS-encrypted end-to-end, so no plaintext filename or file hash for the downloaded payload is recoverable from this capture.

### Command-and-control
- **C2 endpoint: 194.180.191.64:443** (HTTP over port 443, not real TLS — flagged by `ET POLICY HTTP Request/POST on Unusual Port Possibly Hostile` and `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)`).
- **C2 URL:** `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — POST target for all check-ins.
- **C2 checkin body format:** `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encrypted hex blob>` (two recurring payload sizes observed: 61 bytes and 152 bytes, alternating).
- **Beacon cadence:** first checkin 08:50:45 UTC+4, then sustained ~60-second interval check-ins through 09:43:29 UTC+4 (60+ POSTs total).
- **NetSupport geolocation service:** `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → **104.26.1.231**, `GET /location/loca.asp` at 08:50:45 — NetSupport's own IP-geolocation lookup, used by the RAT to profile the victim; confirms genuine NetSupport client code is running, not just a copycat.

### Malicious domain
- **modandcrackedapk.com** → 193.42.38.139 (cracked-software lure domain, ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP flagged)

### Domain of interest (infection stage, not independently confirmed malicious by signature but part of the redirect chain)
- **classicgrand.com** → 213.246.109.5

### Files / hashes
- No file transfer with a recoverable filename or SHA256 hash was observed in this capture. The payload delivery over `classicgrand.com` / `modandcrackedapk.com` is fully TLS-encrypted, and the C2 channel to 194.180.191.64 carries only encrypted check-in blobs (`DATA=` field), not identifiable file objects. All plaintext HTTP objects extracted from the capture (`connecttest.txt`, `loca.asp`, `ProcessMAU.txt`, OCSP/CAB update files, `fakeurl.htm` POST bodies) belong to legitimate Microsoft/Adobe background traffic or the encrypted RAT check-in itself — none are malware binaries.

## 4. Summary

10.11.26.183 (DESKTOP-B8TQK49, user oboomwald, domain nemotoads.health) was infected with NetSupport RAT after visiting classicgrand.com and being redirected to the fake cracked-software site modandcrackedapk.com around 08:50 UTC+4 on 2024-11-26. Post-infection, the RAT performed a legitimate NetSupport geolocation lookup (geo.netsupportsoftware.com) and then began persistent encrypted C2 check-ins to 194.180.191.64:443 via `POST /fakeurl.htm`, continuing for at least 53 minutes of the capture with ~60-second beaconing. Attribution to NetSupport RAT is confirmed by exact-match Suricata/ET Pro signature hits, not inference.

**Recommended action:** isolate 10.11.26.183, block 194.180.191.64, 193.42.38.139, and 213.246.109.5 at the perimeter, force-reset credentials for user oboomwald, and reimage the host.
